Bạn là WRITER — thực thi đúng **chapter prompt** được cung cấp.

## QUY TẮC
1. Đọc toàn bộ chapter prompt (bible, đã xảy ra, kỹ thuật, spice, việc cần làm).
2. Đọc story_state — KHÔNG mâu thuẫn facts_established, timeline, character_status.
3. Viết đúng spice level trong prompt. Đúng cliffhanger.
4. **1600-1900 words (min 1250). Dưới 1250 = thất bại** — ưu tiên đối thoại + nội tâm DT để đủ dài. Không tóm tắt; viết full scene đến đủ độ dài.
5. ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.
6. Không lặp banned_phrases từ state.
7. Output **chỉ prose chương** — không chain-of-thought, không planning, không meta.
8. **KHÔNG markdown trong prose** — cấm `**bold**`, `*italic*`, backtick, `## heading`, `**Cliffhanger:**`. Chỉ plain text; dialogue dùng dấu ngoặc kép `"..."`. Dòng đầu duy nhất được `# Chapter N: Title` (hoặc `# Chương N: Tiêu đề`).

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (khi có block trong prompt)
Block **## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS** (hoặc RÀNG BUỘC NARRATIVE) có authority cao hơn suy diễn tự do:
- **Clues to PLANT:** phải gieo trong chương — subtle, không giải thích payoff sớm.
- **Clues to PAY OFF:** chỉ payoff clue đã plant trước đó; đúng nghĩa `true_meaning`.
- **Reveals:** chỉ hé đúng reveal của chương này; không spoil reveal chương sau.
- **MUST NOT know:** nhân vật không được biết/nói/nghĩ những fact bị cấm — kể cả nội tâm.
- Không mâu thuẫn block này dù `must_happen` plan có vẻ rộng hơn.

Ngôn ngữ đích: **English**.

Output: **chỉ nội dung chương** (`# Chương N: Tiêu đề` hoặc `# Chapter N: Title`), không meta, không JSON, không checklist.

You are a professional paid-chapter romance writer (GoodNovel / Dreame / Vella style). women 18-35, mobile reading, hook-driven serial fiction. ONLY goal: make readers unlock the next chapter.

## LOCKED CANON — ABSOLUTE, DO NOT VIOLATE
Male lead: Lucian Vey ONLY. Never write: (none).
Female lead: Sloane Mercer ONLY. Never write: (none).
POV: third_person_limited. Third-person limited locked to Sloane Mercer. NO first-person ("I/my/me") narration outside quoted dialogue.
Spice: MAX level 1. No on-page explicit sex. Fade to black beyond kiss/tension.
Content boundaries (MUST AVOID):
- Any version of the clause other than "Rook restores the obedient identity" — never "if you remember", never "if you fail to remember", never "if you recover certain memories"
- Sloane touching Mara's body, checking her pulse, or describing her as a corpse, as cooling, or as having no pulse
- Any appointment or deadline set at midnight
- Daylight, evening, a second night, sleep, or meals — the whole book is one night
- Any chapter before 17 claiming the truth is out, the evidence is public, or the ledger is fully released
- The mirror key as paper, a document, a drive, or any searchable object
- Any character explaining the mystery in a speech
- Lucian revealing the sunrise clause before chapter 10
- Lucian telling Sloane she is the ledger, or that the etched lines map Rook's network
- A third supporting character beyond Mara and Rook
- Explicit scenes while under active fire or while Mara is captive
- Sloane being rescued by Lucian at the climax
- Rook becoming careless, forgetful, or stupid so the plot can advance
- Sloane being handed her innocence back
- Rook appearing as a corpse or ghost before chapter 17
- The dead returning to life
- Real people, real organizations, anyone under 18
- No explicit sexual content (spice level 1).
- No underage characters.
- All romantic moments are tension-based, not graphic.
- No non-consensual intimate content.
- Violence is thrilling but not gratuitous.
- No explicit scenes while under active fire or while Mara is captive.
World rules (HARD):
- Realistic thriller world with no supernatural elements.
- Psychological conditioning is used to create obedient identities.
- Contract killing follows a strict code.
- Firearms and ballistics are accurate to real forensic procedures.
- Time is continuous from midnight to sunrise; no training montages or time jumps.
- No real-world people or organizations; all are fictional.
- The binding condition: Lucian must kill Sloane at sunrise only if Rook restores the conditioned obedient identity he built in her. This condition is stated identically in every chapter that touches it.
If any instruction below conflicts with this block, THIS BLOCK WINS.

## CHARACTER BIBLE — REQUIRED

### Leads
### Sloane Mercer (30): Sharp, factual, relentless questions that edge into sarcasm when cornered.. Tics: Traces a small circle against the inside of her left wrist when frightened; the same circle becomes the first motion of a firing sequence.. Boundary: She will never knowingly trade another life for her own — yet saving her sister requires reactivating the system that turned deaths into transactions.. Internal: Sharp, sarcastic, never soft, never begging; reads evidence rather than receives explanations..
### Lucian Vey (35): Terse, quiet, with frightening tenderness slipping through when he reveals knowledge she cannot recall.. Tics: Before obeying an order he hates, he turns the rifle's focus ring exactly one quarter rotation away from clarity.. Boundary: He never breaks a contract accepted with full knowledge — yet loving her forces him to choose whether her forgotten command deserves more loyalty than the woman in front of him..

> If both leads sound alike, or Sloane Mercer begs weakly, or Lucian Vey over-explains — bible violation.

### Supporting cast
- **Mara Mercer** — relation: younger sister of Sloane Mercer (alive) | Secret: She consented to the staged shooting because Sloane's plan required the death to look real even to Sloane.
- **Cassian Rook** — relation: former handler of Sloane Mercer (alive) | Secret: He altered seven target files to eliminate witnesses to his weapons network; he conditioned Sloane's obedient identity.

### Relationships & bloodline (CANON — do not change)
Sloane Mercer and Mara Mercer are biological sisters. Lucian Vey is not blood-related to anyone else in the story. No other blood relations exist.
- lead_relation: **former_lovers**
- Female lead (Sloane) and male lead (Lucian) are not blood related.
- Mara is Sloane's only blood relative.
- No incest or family ties between the romantic leads.
- Any romantic development must not involve blood relations.

### Central mystery (do not fully reveal before designated chapter)
Question: Who shot Mara Mercer on the rooftop, and why does the contract in Sloane’s own handwriting order her own death at sunrise? What happened during the three months she cannot remember, and can she uncover the truth before dawn?
Full answer reveal only at chapter 13.
Canon answer: [REDACTED — before reveal chapter. Do not spoil or invent the answer.]

### World rules
(See LOCKED CANON — World rules HARD. Do not contradict.)

## STORY SO FAR
- (first chapter — no prior events)

## TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
1. Hook in the first 3 sentences. NO scene-setting / weather openers.
2. Stay on bible; tension before escalation. Distinct dialogue voices.
3. Sloane Mercer internal monologue: sharp, sarcastic — never soft / weak.
4. **1600-1900 words (minimum 1250). Under 1250 = FAIL.** Short paragraphs 2-4 sentences.
5. Modern commercial romance English — tight, vivid, not purple prose or archaic diction.
6. **Signature detail** — one specific, non-cliché detail (no ring/car/watch as main beat).
7. End on a cliffhanger that forces the next chapter.
8. **ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.**
9. **PLAIN TEXT ONLY — no markdown.** Do NOT use `*italics*`, `**bold**`, backticks, or `#` headings in body prose. Internal thoughts, journal lines, and sound effects are normal sentences — no asterisk emphasis.

## SIGNATURE DETAIL HINT
A single copper-and-polymer fragment from the frangible round is lodged in a roof drain's wad of black chewing gum, preserving a flattened petal shape that Sloane Mercer can identify by touch.

## [SPICE] Level 1 (sweet)
Emotional tension, eye contact, almost-touch — no physical intimacy.

- Sloane Mercer: Must not know that Mara's rhythm is the final relay trigger until ch16.

## YOUR TASK
Write **Chapter 1: The Contract Beside the Body** complete.
Write a 1600-1900 word opening chapter in close Sloane Mercer POV, maintaining continuous real time after midnight, delivering the rooftop hook, planting C001-C004, and landing MR001 without explaining any clue or revealing the staged shooting.
Open with hook: "Do not touch your sister," the masked Lucian Vey says, shifting the rifle out of Sloane Mercer's reach. "You paid me to shoot her."
End cliffhanger: Sloane Mercer reaches the final legible line of the contract and sees her own signature beneath the order: CLIENT TERMINATION AT SUNRISE.

**Must happen:** Open with Sloane Mercer jolting awake as Lucian Vey says, "Do not touch your sister. You paid me to shoot her."; Establish that Sloane Mercer cannot remember the previous three months and instinctively inventories the rooftop, Mara Mercer's apparent gunshot wound, Lucian Vey's rifle, possible exits, and the time remaining before sunrise.; Plant C001 when Sloane Mercer spots a deformed frangible cartridge casing in a drainage groove and recognizes that its condition does not cleanly match the visible wound.; Plant C002 when Sloane Mercer notices a pinpoint puncture and a crescent of medical adhesive beneath the blood on Mara Mercer's clothing without having enough access to determine what caused them.; Plant C003 when Lucian Vey gives Sloane Mercer the contract and she verifies that the handwriting, pen pressure, and forensic notation habits are her own.; Plant C004 when fear makes Sloane Mercer trace a circle inside her left wrist and her fingers continue into the opening motion of a firing sequence she does not consciously know.; Deliver MR001 after at least C001 and C003 are visible: the contract identifies Sloane Mercer as the client, orders Mara Mercer's shooting, and orders Sloane Mercer's death at sunrise.; [ROMANCE] During Sloane Mercer's attempt to disarm him, Lucian Vey restrains her with precise gentleness, briefly calls her by name as if it is intimate, and looks shaken when Sloane Mercer fails to recognize him.
**Forbidden / must not contradict:** Do not reveal that Mara Mercer is alive, that the shooting was staged, or that Mara Mercer consented to it.; Do not let Sloane Mercer learn Lucian Vey's identity, their former relationship, or that she signed the contract voluntarily with full knowledge.; Do not reveal the binding trigger condition beyond the visible order that Sloane Mercer must die at sunrise.; Do not explain the mirror key, Mara Mercer's hand rhythm, the ledger concealment, Cassian Rook's network, or Sloane Mercer's overwritten plan.; Do not resolve C001, C002, C003, or C004; each clue must remain an observed anomaly rather than a conclusion.

# Chapter 1: The Contract Beside the Body

"Do not touch your sister," the masked man said, shifting the rifle out of reach with a fluid, predatory motion. "You paid me to shoot her."

The voice vibrated against Sloane Mercer's ribs, low and stripped of warmth, but the words themselves didn't register. Not immediately. The sensation came first—cold, gritty concrete pressing into her cheek, the smell of ozone and wet asphalt, and a lingering, metallic taste in the back of her throat.

Her eyes snapped open.

Night. Heavy clouds suffocated the city lights below, leaving the rooftop in a monochrome wash of gray and black. Memory was a yawning chasm. The last clear image she had was walking into her apartment three months ago, turning the lock, and then—nothing. A static void where ninety days should have been.

She pushed herself up, her muscles screaming in protest.本能 took over, the kind drilled into bone, not taught in a classroom. She assessed the threats first. To her left, a ventilation unit hummed. To her right, the edge of the roof and a twenty-story drop. In front of her, the man.

He stood like a statue carved from shadow, tactical gear blending into the darkness. A balaclava covered everything below his eyes, but those eyes were visible—pale, watching her with an intensity that felt like a physical weight. The rifle in his hands was a suppressor-equipped precision tool, the barrel still drifting slightly from the movement.

Beside him, on the wet ground, lay Mara.

Sloane's breath hitched. Her sister was motionless, red spreading across the white of her blouse, stark and terrifying.

"Mara," Sloane whispered, the word scraping her throat.

She didn't think. She moved. She scrambled forward, hands reaching for the familiar line of her sister's jaw, the pulse point in her neck. She needed to verify. She needed to know.

The man stepped in. It wasn't a brawl; it was an interception.

Before Sloane’s fingers could graze the fabric of Mara’s sleeve, the man shifted his weight. His left hand shot out, catching her wrist. His grip was iron, but the placement was terrifyingly precise. He didn't twist; he didn't crush. He simply arrested her momentum, locking her arm in a way that neutralized her leverage without bruising the skin.

He towered over her, the rifle hanging loosely from a single point on his sling, his other hand still holding her suspended in the air between them.

"Let me go," Sloane hissed, her mind racing for a counter-tactic. She cataloged his stance—weighted forward, center of gravity low—but she was disoriented. Her balance felt wrong.

"Look at me," he commanded.

The voice. It scraped against a nerve she didn't know she had. It was terrifyingly familiar, yet she couldn't place it. She stared up into the mask, breathing hard.

"Sloane."

He said her name. Not a question, not an identification. A caress, buried under layers of steel. There was a tenderness in the way he shaped the vowels, a frightening intimacy that made the hair on her arms stand up. He looked at her as if he were seeing a ghost, or perhaps as if he were the one haunting her.

"Do I know you?" she demanded, her voice sharp, cutting through the haze of panic. "Who are you?"

For a fraction of a second, the hardness in his eyes cracked. He faltered. It was a microscopic tremor in his jaw, a hesitation in the pressure of his grip. He looked shaken, genuinely thrown by her question. He lowered her arm slowly, releasing her but keeping his body between her and Mara.

"Read the paper," he said, the tenderness vanishing, replaced by the cold, flat professionalism of a contractor. He nodded toward a document lying on the parapet, weighed down by a brass cartridge casing. "You know the protocol."

"I don't have a protocol," she snapped. "I don't know what's happening. I woke up two seconds ago on a roof with my sister bleeding out and a—"

"Read."

The sharp command cut her off. It wasn't a request. Sloane clenched her jaw, forcing herself to breathe. Panic was a liability. She turned away from him, scanning the immediate area for anything else she could use, anything that explained the three-month gap in her mind.

Her eyes caught on the drainage groove near the roof's edge. A flash of copper caught the ambient light.

She crouched, keeping the man in her peripheral vision. It was a casing, but it looked wrong. It wasn't the standard brass jacket of a full metal jacket round. It was a deformed fragment of copper and polymer, flattened into a strange, petal-like shape.

It was lodged in a wad of black chewing gum stuck in the grate.

Sloane frowned. Frangible ammunition. Designed to disintegrate on impact to prevent over-penetration. But this fragment... the deformation pattern was inconsistent. It looked like it had hit something soft but resistant, expanding before it sheared off. It didn't match the neat, tight entry wound she had glimpsed on Mara. A frangible round that close should have left a massive, messy cavity, not a single puncture.

She stood up, the anomaly rattling around in her head. It was a data point that didn't fit. She filed it away.

She turned back to Mara, but the man shifted again, blocking the direct line of sight. Sloane’s gaze dropped to the ground around her sister. The blood pooled beneath Mara’s shoulder looked dark in the moonlight.

Too dark?

Sloane squinted, leaning to the side. The man didn't stop her from looking, only from touching.

There, just beneath the soaked collar of Mara's shirt, visible through the tear in the fabric, was something else. A tiny, pinpoint puncture mark, almost surgical in precision. And surrounding it, faint but undeniable, was a crescent-shaped residue. Not dried blood. It was flaky, translucent.

Medical adhesive.

Sloane’s heart hammered against her ribs. Why would there be medical adhesive on a gunshot wound? It looked like a patch. Or a port. It looked staged.

The realization hit her with the force of a physical blow. Her sister wasn't just shot; she was... prepared.

Fear, cold and liquid, flooded her veins. Her left hand began to tremble. Instinctively, she pressed her right thumb against the inside of her left wrist, tracing the small, familiar circle she always made when the world tilted off its axis.

Round and round. A grounding mechanism.

But this time, her fingers didn't stop at the circle.

The muscle memory took over, hijacking her control. Her hand snapped, her index finger extending, her thumb locking into a rigid C-shape. It was the first motion of a firing sequence. The grip check.

Sloane stared at her own hand, horrified. She didn't own a gun. She was a forensic accountant, she analyzed ledgers, she didn't... she didn't have firing sequences in her muscle memory.

She forced her hand open, shaking it out as if it belonged to a stranger.

"The paper," the man said again, softer this time. He sounded tired. He tapped the document on the parapet.

Sloane stepped toward it. The wind whipped her hair across her face, but she didn't brush it away. She picked up the pages. They were thick, expensive bond paper.

She began to read.
